fanTake: The Patriots absolutely throttled Pittsburgh at home, 20-3, in a game that felt less like a competitive affair and more like a necessary cleansing. Our defense was genuinely exceptional—holding the Steelers to a field goal while generating the kind of suffocating pressure that reminds you why this team has weathered so many storms. Offensively, we weren't exactly lighting it up (that negative EPA/play is a sobering reminder), but two touchdowns and two field goals proved sufficient when your defense is playing like it did. Rhamondre Stevenson was our MVP in win probability terms, which tells you we leaned on the ground game and played complementary football. It wasn't pretty, but in October, sometimes ugly wins are exactly what you need.
